_comment: Tuning for the CLASSIC drillr carousel. Everything the template needs lives
here, so a change to the look or the words is a config edit rather than a
code edit. See README.md.
This is a separate generator from drillr-social, not a mode of it. That one
writes fresh copy for every post; this one does not write copy at all.
THE TEXT IS CONSTANT. The original carousels all carried the same seven
lines and only the photos changed between them, so that is what this
reproduces: the words below are the whole script, and a new carousel is the
same slides with different pictures. Edit a line here and every carousel
made afterwards carries the new wording.
width/height are the OUTER frame. The off-white band inside it is sized by
render.py from the reference aspect - do not try to set it here.
_script: The seven slides, in order: the words on each one and where its picture
text:   the headline. Slide 7 also has `footer`, the line under the photo.
image:  `pool:<path>` takes the next image from that folder, or a plain
path for a single fixed file. `aside` is the second picture on
The wording is the original set's, with two typos fixed: `Drill` was `Drillr`
in two headlines, and 'Drill gives, you tips' had a stray comma.
Keep each headline under about 60 characters. Past that it wraps to a third
line of heavy type and pushes the screenshot off the bottom of the slide -
`doctor` checks this and will tell you.
Each of the four app screens is a FOLDER of captures, not one file, and a
carousel takes the least-recently-used one from each. That is what stops
slides 3-6 being the same image on every post - see assets/screens/README.md.

script.text: Top apps you need to improve your football skills
Drillr builds your weekly plan with drills for your position
Drillr gives you tips to master the basics of the game
Drillr builds you a personalized meal plan
Drillr tracks your progress every step of the way

_comment: Every `pool:` in the script above. Images are picked least-recently-used
first and the choice is recorded in state/pools-used.json.
backgrounds/landscape carries the hook and the CTA photo - both sit in a
wide slot, so a 9:16 wallpaper lands there badly. backgrounds/portrait
carries the player shot beside the progress screenshot. Kept apart rather
than cropped from one pool because the template shows each photo at its
own aspect.
cooldownDays: warn when a photo comes round again inside this many days.
It is a signal that the pool is too thin, which matters more here than in
the sibling tool - the words never change, so the pictures are the only
thing keeping two posts from reading as the same post.
noCooldown: pools that are SUPPOSED to come round quickly, matched by
path prefix. A screen slot holds a handful of real device captures, so
warning every time one repeats would just be noise.
OFF until the app clears TikTok's audit - same blocker as drillr-social,
and the same account, so clearing it once clears it for both.
urlPrefix must be a domain verified in the TikTok developer portal.
privacyLevel stays SELF_ONLY while unaudited: TikTok forces private on
unaudited clients anyway, and asking for PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE just fails.
